summary: Ad-hoc SIEM slice subsetting for legal hold with custodian-signed certificate and timebound retention exception
description: Issue summary: Customer requests an on-demand subset (slice) of audit events to satisfy a court-ordered legal hold. They need per-field redaction/pseudonymization for PII, a custodian-signed certificate asserting receipt, and a timebound retention exception (retain for 2 years instead of standard 90 days). Impact: customer cannot complete legal process without the partial export; high regulatory risk. Environment: production activity ledger spanning multi-tenant audit store in us-east. Request details: deliver a chronologically-ordered NDJSON slice for tenant 'fsb-prod' across the time window 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-02-15T23:59:59Z, include resume token for replay, include per-record HMAC (customer-supplied key material allowed), include a manifest that maps original field names to pseudonymized identifiers and lists redaction reasons. Produce a custodian-signed certificate (PDF) that we can attach to the legal binder. Preferred delivery: encrypted S3 presigned URL to a one-off bucket with object-lock enabled for the two-year window. Secondary delivery option: Azure Event Grid deliverable if S3 is not available.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer raised request via security questionnaire and legal team (attached in initial ticket).
2) Support validated customer entitlement and legal hold request.
3) Requested technical parameters: time window, field allowlist, pseudonymization mode (hmac vs reversible pseudonym), custodian certificate signer identity.
4) Attempted to run on-demand export via internal playbook; export job failed initially due to missing per-tenant key binding for HMAC.
5) Created linked internal ticket to provision ephemeral KMS binding and object-lock bucket.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: export fails due to missing per-tenant KMS binding — confirmed by error trace-6f4d.
Checked export orchestration logs (k8s job logs) — HMAC step failed before binding; after binding job completed and post-processing created manifest file alongside NDJSON.

Reviewed object-lock policy: S3 bucket 'redwood-adhoc-deliveries' had object-lock enabled for one-off deliveries; retention window override required explicit approval from legal ops (approval granted 2026-03-11 by Legal Ops ticket LGL-778).
Confluence playbook referenced for manual exports: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Manual+On-Demand+Audit+Export+Playbook
resolution: Workaround delivered: one-off encrypted NDJSON bundle uploaded to presigned S3 URL with object-lock and two-year retention; custodian_receipt_draft.pdf supplied for customer to countersign. Field mapping adjusted per customer's request and new manifest posted. Follow-up: engineering to add a first-class 'on-demand slice API' that supports per-tenant HMAC, custodian certificate generation, and retention-exception flag. Tracking work created as INT-43921 and design doc PR at https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-export/pull/563. Legal ops confirmed retention exception recorded in compliance ledger.
